devin: Quick brain-dump — we need to pick a direction for the hosting adapter surface. Two poles: a thin adapter (handshake, routing, auth tokens only) vs a rich sidecar (translation, telemetry enrichment, local fallback logic). I'm leaning thin for Private (min surface, less ops), richer for Hosted/Dedicated to keep observability. Thoughts?
maria: +1 on minimizing surface in Private. But how do we handle KMS/HSM integration if adapter is thin? Private deployments often require KMS in customer VPC.
aj: If adapter is thin we push KMS calls to control plane or runtime? That changes trust boundaries. Also telemetry: do we accept opaque logs or require structured spans?
sarah: From latency SLO perspective, thin adapter is better (fewer hops). But richer sidecar lets us do local prefix caching and batching hints which can improve cost for high-throughput tenants. Tradeoff. :thinking:
devin: Good points. My rough trade matrix:
- Thin adapter pros: smaller API, easier certs, fewer secrets in our plane.
- Thin adapter cons: moves complexity to runtime/control-plane or client, harder to get consistent telemetry.
- Rich sidecar pros: local optimizations (KV cache reuse, batching, prefetch), can normalize fallbacks across environments.
- Rich sidecar cons: bigger upgrade surface, more secrets to manage, version skew risks.
I sketched a minimal RPC surface that might meet both:
```
service AdapterHandshake {
  rpc AnnounceClient(AnnounceRequest) returns (AnnounceAck);
  rpc TokenExchange(TokenRequest) returns (TokenResponse);
  // optional capability advert: batching, cache, kms-proxy
  rpc Capabilities(Empty) returns (CapabilitySet);
}
```
We mark capabilities optional so Private can implement only handshake + token exchange.
ben: If we go capability flags we need health and circuit-breaker semantics per-capability. Otherwise a Private runtime that claims caching but actually doesn't will break assumptions.
maria: +1 on capability health. Also: add a `telemetry_endpoint_hint` field so the sidecar can emit to local observability when present, otherwise falls back to central. That avoids forcing Private to push traces into our hosted pipeline.
aj: For auth, consider two modes: `passthrough` (client signs to customer KMS, adapter only routes) vs `proxy` (adapter signs on behalf using delegated creds). Document both in the API and require explicit capability flags.
sarah: Regarding caching: adapter should expose a cache-key contract and invalidation hints. Keep this as metadata not enforced behavior. That way Private can ignore it. But we must be careful: some runtime optimizations rely on deterministic keys.
devin: Agreed. Also thinking about rollout mechanics: default to thin adapter in the Minimal compatibility profile. Rich sidecar in Enhanced profile. Feature flags for rollout: `adapter.profile=minimal|enhanced`.
ops-bot: Related RFC link: https://confluence.redwood/infra/adapter-profiles (posted by automation)
ben: Integration tests: create a matrix that validates each capability flag with synthetic load: auth modes x caching x telemetry. Add a fake Private harness to prove behavior when capability absent.
maria: Ops and security want an explicit audit path for TokenExchange and any KMS-proxy operations. Even if adapter is thin, we need an audit webhook.
aj: Also think about schema evolution: capability set should be a semvered JSON map, not freeform strings. Enables compatibility checks at handshake.
sarah: One more ops constraint — sidecar should expose a local admin endpoint for debug (only on loopback) with strict RBAC. Private teams may want to inspect without elevating network surface.
devin: Next steps I propose: 1) I'll author a small RFC with the provisional protobuf and capability matrix. 2) AJ and Maria, can you sketch the auth/KMS modes and required audit events? 3) Ben/SRE, please draft the integration test matrix. We'll keep it lightweight and iterate.
maria: I can do auth/KMS sketch by EOD tomorrow.
aj: Will take audit + proxy security considerations.
sarah: I'll add latency/regression tests to the matrix.
ben: I'll spin up the fake Private harness and share early.
ops-bot: Note: tagging #security-team and #sre for review.
